title: The Daily Five
dek: Five questions on Israeli sport, from a Wimbledon first to a fresh Champions League upset.

questions.question: Who partnered Andy Ram to the 2006 Wimbledon mixed doubles title, making him Israel's first Grand Slam champion?
questions.explanation: Ram and Vera Zvonareva beat Bob Bryan and Venus Williams 6-3, 6-2 in the final on Centre Court on 8 July 2006.

questions.question: Which country won gold at the 2008 Chess Olympiad in Dresden, finishing one point ahead of Israel's silver-medal squad?
questions.explanation: Armenia took gold with 19 match points, one ahead of Israel's 18, despite losing 2½–1½ to Israel during the event.

questions.question: By what aggregate score did Hapoel Beer Sheva eliminate Red Star Belgrade from Champions League qualifying?
questions.explanation: Beer Sheva won 1-0 away in the first leg and 2-0 at home in the second, for a 3-0 aggregate victory.

questions.question: Which Premier League club agreed a fee for Israel international Anan Khalaili, set to become the most expensive Israeli player in history?
questions.explanation: Palace agreed roughly £21m with Union Saint-Gilloise for Khalaili, beating out Everton, Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

questions.question: Ariel Berkovich, newly promoted to Maccabi Ironi Ramat Gan's senior squad, is the grandson of which Maccabi Tel Aviv and Israel basketball legend?
questions.explanation: Ariel is the grandson of Miki Berkovich, a FIBA Hall of Famer who won 16 Israeli championships and two European Champions Cups with Maccabi Tel Aviv.
